tasks.short: Contact housekeeping or maintenance about guest problems.

steps.what: Hear problems guests report at the desk.
Choose housekeeping or maintenance for the problem.
Contact housekeeping or maintenance staff by phone.
Log the problem after the clerk made contact.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk hears the problem, chooses housekeeping or maintenance, and contacts them by phone. A short log on {OPS_SYSTEM} records that the call was made. The call is not replaced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The contact was a phone call, and the same problem was then written in a book.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system can hold a one-line log after the clerk has made the call.
tasks.still_hard: The guest is waiting, the fault may be urgent, and the right person is whoever is on duty.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the guest and making the call stay with the clerk.
tasks.altitude: The call stays. The log after the call is a little shorter, and the clerk still checks it.

reach.task: Attend a problem the desk reported
reach.learn: Act on the phone call from the desk clerk

evidence.claim: A one-line problem log can be stored after the clerk has contacted the team.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the guest reports a problem and ends when the log is written. The repair itself stays outside it.
The log fields are room, team, and a short fault. The clerk writes them after the call. There is no automatic contact.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree.
Upkeep is keeping the duty numbers the clerk already uses.
unknowns: Whether maintenance already has its own request book the desk must use.
Which faults the clerk may log without calling first.
research_questions: Does maintenance require a phone call, a written request, or both?
Which faults are urgent enough that the log waits until after the call?

already_counted.description: Logging the problem after the call stays partly in that step

incremental.description: Keep the duty numbers the clerk already calls

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case keeps the hearing and the phone call in full. The low end moves only the short log, and only when that log is still a second writing. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Clean the lobby, restock supplies, and water plants.

steps.what: Clean and maintain the lobby and common areas.
Restocking supplies guests use in the lobby.
Watering plants in the common areas.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk cleans the lobby, restocks supplies, and waters the plants. No system takes any of that work. Nothing is filed in its place.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is physical and was never a screen task, so there was nothing to connect.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new makes cleaning, restocking, or watering a desk task for software.
tasks.still_hard: The lobby still has to be cleaned by a person between guests.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk, or whoever is on the desk, still does this with their hands.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. Cleaning, restocking, and watering stay as they are.

reach.task: Cover the lobby when the desk is with a guest
reach.learn: The lobby work stays a person's job

evidence.claim: Cleaning a lobby, restocking supplies, and watering plants are physical work and stay with a person.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the lobby needs attention and ends when it is done. There is no record and no send.
No fields are stored. There is no fallback because there is no screen step.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree. No part of it is counted as saved.
Upkeep is zero because no list, code, or screen is added.
unknowns: Whether this property still expects the desk clerk to clean the lobby.
Whether a housekeeper already does the plants and the supplies.
research_questions: Does the desk clerk still clean the lobby at this property?
Who restocks the lobby supplies today?

already_counted.description: Cleaning the lobby stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: No screen or list is added, so there is nothing to keep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case and the centre are the same. Cleaning, restocking, and watering do not shrink, so the saving is zero. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Stamp, sort, and rack incoming mail and messages.

steps.what: Stamp incoming mail as it arrives.
Sort incoming messages into the mail rack.
Rack incoming mail for the named guest.
Note a message that cannot be racked.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk stamps, sorts, and racks the mail by hand. {OPS_SYSTEM} holds a note only when a piece cannot be matched to a guest. The racking itself stays physical.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mail was already handled by hand, and an unmatched piece was written on a slip.
tasks.enabler_now: An unmatched name can be typed once, beside the stays the property system already holds.
tasks.still_hard: Handwriting on an envelope, a guest who has not arrived, and a package that will not fit in the rack all stay physical.
tasks.human_edge: Stamping, sorting, and racking stay with the clerk.
tasks.altitude: The mail handling stays. Only a note for a piece that cannot be racked is a little shorter.

reach.learn: The rack is still filled by the desk clerk

evidence.claim: An unmatched mail item can be noted against the stays the property system already holds.

assumptions: The workflow starts when mail arrives and ends when it is in the rack or noted as unmatched. Opening guests' mail stays outside it.
The note fields are the name on the piece and the date. The clerk writes them. Matched mail is not entered.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree.
Upkeep is small: the note uses the guest names already on stays.
unknowns: How much of the mail is still physical envelopes.
Whether packages are racked by the desk or by another role.
research_questions: What share of desk mail is still a physical envelope?
Who handles packages that do not fit in the rack?

already_counted.description: Noting an unmatched message stays partly in that step

incremental.description: No new list; unmatched notes use guest names already stored

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case keeps stamping, sorting, and racking in full. The low end moves only the unmatched note, which is a small share of the task. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer hotel inquiries and make recommendations.

steps.what: Look up travel directions and registration hours.
Answer the guest from those hotel services.
Make recommendations regarding dining or entertainment.
Note the recommendation the clerk gave the guest.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk hears the inquiry, looks up hours and directions on a list the property maintains, and answers the guest. Recommendations regarding dining or entertainment stay the clerk's own. No ranking is produced, and no answer is sent unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hours and directions were in a folder, and the clerk repeated them from memory or from a card.
tasks.enabler_now: A maintained list of hours, registration times, and directions can be opened at the desk.
tasks.still_hard: The guest's question is specific, and a recommendation depends on what they just asked.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk chooses the answer and the recommendation. A list does not speak for the desk.
tasks.altitude: Looking up hours and directions is shorter. Answering the guest and making the recommendation stay with the clerk.

reach.task: Ask the desk for a place to eat
reach.learn: The recommendation comes from the desk clerk, not from a ranking

evidence.claim: Hours, registration times, and directions can be kept on a list the clerk opens while the guest is there.
A recommendation to a guest is the clerk's own answer. A ranking of guests, or an unattended reply, is not used.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the guest asks and ends when the clerk has answered. Booking a tour or a taxi is a separate task.

The list fields are service name, hours, and a short direction. The property maintains them. If a fact is missing, the clerk says they do not know. The recommendation is spoken by the clerk and is not generated.
The prior treats the task as amplify. The steps disagree with any model that would choose the recommendation. The list is configured text, and the answer stays with the clerk.
Upkeep is keeping hours and directions on that list.
unknowns: Who maintains the list of hours and local directions.
Whether the property wants any recommendation written down, or only spoken.
research_questions: Who keeps the list of hotel services, hours, and directions?
Should a recommendation be written on the stay, or only spoken?

already_counted.description: Looking up hours and directions stays partly in that step

incremental.description: Keep hours and directions on the desk list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the list is thin, the lookup saves little and the low end falls, because the answer and the recommendation were never counted as saved. No ranking is introduced in either case. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Calling housekeeping, cleaning the lobby, racking the mail, and recommending a place to eat stay with the clerk. A list of hours can be opened faster. Nothing ranks guests or answers for the desk.
reach: A guest hears a recommendation from the desk clerk, not from a ranking
skills_to_grow: Answering from a maintained list of hours and directions
Making a recommendation without a ranking
Leaving lobby cleaning and mail racking as physical work
role.ambitious_version: Hours and directions are on a list the clerk can open, and every recommendation is still the clerk's own.
